name: Browser saved address and card autofill
plain: Chrome and Safari offer saved addresses and cards to fill checkout forms.
meaning: Gives a site a user's address, phone and card after the person picks them in a browser prompt.

web.api: Standard form fields plus autocomplete tokens; Payment Request API for cards

access.prompt_ui: Browser popup listing saved profiles and cards
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Chrome and Safari offer saved addresses and cards to fill checkout forms.

fields.name: shippingAddress
fields.range: country, region, city, postalCode, addressLine, recipient, phone

fields.name: card details
fields.precision: needs CVC re entry in Chrome

limits.headline: Can offer your saved addresses and cards to fill a form, if you pick them
limits.user_action: You tap a form field and choose a saved address or card from the list.
can: Fill a name, address or phone number from your saved ones
Fill a saved card number in a checkout form
cannot: See your saved cards or addresses before you pick them
Fill your card's security code without asking in many browsers
Fill anything if you turned autofill off
limits.differs: Chrome and Safari fill saved addresses and cards. Firefox fills addresses, but cards only partly.

story.what_it_is: Your browser can fill saved addresses and cards at checkout after you choose them.

marketing.name: Autofill in Chrome
marketing.pitch: Chrome's help page says Chrome can fill saved addresses, cards and passwords so forms go faster.

story.for_you: A small menu offers your saved address or card. You tap it and the form fills in, without you typing.
story.for_makers: Makers get faster checkouts and fewer errors, so more people finish buying. A skimmer script can try to steal the filled values, so shops must guard the page.

use_cases.example: You buy shoes on a store and your address and card fill in one tap.
A takeout site fills your delivery address and card.
A booking site fills your name, phone and card.
A streaming site fills a card for a free trial that you then forget.
A skimmer script on a checkout page tries to copy the filled card.
A bank page fills your billing address.

technical_bounds: Address returned only after user chooses
